correctness.rationale: The Petersen graph has six perfect matchings; each graph edge belongs to exactly two and each matching pair meets in exactly one edge, with no triple facet intersection. Hence X is six 4-simplices pairwise glued at distinct vertices. The explicit retraction using the second-largest barycentric coordinate b(x) and weights max(x_i-b(x),0) maps each facet continuously and permutation-equivariantly onto its vertex-star and fixes its vertices, so glues to an S5-equivariant strong deformation retraction onto subdivided K6. The graph chain boundary on exterior square of Z[F] has kernel wedge^2 of its rank-five augmentation lattice, giving H1=Z^10 as an integral S5-module. Character calculations yield rational S^(3,1,1) plus S^(2,1,1,1); orbit graph counts give contractible S5/A5 quotients and C5 quotient wedge of two circles.
